name: Block Billing
description: Lumping or aggregation of multiple tasks into a single narrative entry with a sum total of time instead of listing each task and the precise related time.
notes: Must interpret if multiple distinct tasks are lumped together in one narrative.

name: Communication Inspecificity
description: Outside counsel's time entries regarding electronic or telephonic communications should identify the subject matter of the communication and name the counterparty to it.
notes: Need to see if comms describe subject and counterparty; semantic review needed.

name: Cross Matter Churning
description: Timekeeper records time for handling substantially the same task in the same time frame in two or more separate matters or invoices.
notes: Compare similar tasks by same TK across matters/dates; requires text similarity.

name: Cross Matter Hourly Maximum
description: TK bills more than 8 hours in a day spread across more than 1 invoice
notes: Sum hours per TK per day across invoices and check if >8 and >1 invoice.

name: Duplicative Charge
description: The identical line item charge appears twice in the same invoice.
notes: Detect duplicate lines on same invoice via date, narrative, hours, and amount.

name: Delinquent Time
description: All line item time entries should be dated within 61 days of the invoice date.
notes: Compute difference between line date and invoice date and compare to 61 days.

name: Embedded Time Discrepancy
description: Discrepancies found with time notations embedded in line narratives.
notes: Need to parse time mentions in text and compare to billed units; NLP-like parsing.

name: Embedded Time Discrepancy - Over Billing
description: The hours billed for the line is greater than the total of embedded time in the narrative.
notes: Requires extracting embedded times and comparing sum to billed hours for overage.

name: Embedded Time Discrepancy - Under Billing
description: The hours billed for the line is less than the total of embedded time in the narrative.
notes: Same as ETD but detect when embedded time sum exceeds hours billed.

name: Hourly Maximum
description: Timekeepers efficiency levels decrease when working in excess of 8 hours per day.
notes: Sum hours per TK per calendar day on invoice; flag days with total hours >8.

name: Increment Billing
description: Tasks are separated and recorded in multiple time entries in one-tenth hour increments where task is unlikely to take 6 minutes (e.g., left voice message for client, reviewed three sentence e-mail)
notes: Need to interpret task nature and detect many 0.1 entries; semantics required.

name: Indistinguishable Prep Time
description: Timekeeper combines "preparation time and participation time" without specifying the type of preparatory task has been undertaken or time expended for it (e.g., prepare for and participate in all-hands conference call). Inflates time recorded for primary activity undertaken.
notes: Need to detect combined prep and participation without allocation; narrative only.

name: Minimum Billing Increment
description: Time entries should be recorded in 1/10th hour increments.
notes: Check if hours are multiples of 0.1; any other increment violates rule.

name: Non-Business Day Entry
description: Tasks completed on holidays/weekends often completed less efficiently
notes: Can detect weekends via date; holidays need external calendar not provided.

name: No Charge
description: Identifies tasks usually undertaken by outside counsel as a client courtesy or law firm marketing activities (audit response letter, delivery of newsletters/client alerts, attendance at routine board meeting).
notes: Need to infer if activity is courtesy/marketing from narrative content.

name: Overly Verbose
description: Timekeeper disguises simplicity of task undertaken by writing lengthy narrative
notes: Requires judging if length is excessive given task complexity; semantic.

name: Rate Change
description: Identifies an unauthorized change in hourly rate.
notes: Can see rate differences, but authorization baseline not available in fields.

name: Round Hour
description: Timekeeper bills in round hour increments (1.0, 2.0, etc) with a statistically improbable frequency.
notes: Analyze distribution of units per TK and flag high share of whole hours.

name: Repeated Narrative
description: Narrative is repeated verbatim
notes: Detect exact duplicate descriptions across lines; simple string match.

name: Statistically Indefensible Time Entry
description: Time is recorded in increments that defy statistical probabilities
notes: Requires probabilistic modeling of increments beyond simple thresholds.

name: Vague Entry
description: Narrative entry lacks sufficient detail as to nature of task(s) completed
notes: Need to judge specificity of description; semantic understanding required.

name: Wrong Matter
description: Identifies a task that appears to be billed to the wrong matter.
notes: Likely needs cross-matter narrative comparison or external context; NLP.

name: Administrative Activities
description: Administrative functions (billing, scheduling, calendaring, filing) billed at attorney or other legal professional rates.
notes: Need to classify task as admin from text and see if TK is attorney-level.

name: Associate Training
description: Billing by junior legal personnel for activities where primary involvement by junior timekeeper pertains to his or her professional development and internal law firm training purposes.
notes: Narrative must show training/education as primary purpose; needs NLP.

name: Dispersed Work
description: Large number of attorneys handling discrete tasks with little knowledge sharing or workflow management
notes: Requires judgment on what is large and if collaboration exists; vague.

name: Fixed Fee
description: Matter billed under a fixed fee arrangement
notes: No explicit fixed-fee flag; would rely on semantic cues like flat fee.

name: First Year
description: Time is recorded by recent law graduates who operate at a less efficient level.
notes: Need explicit year/admit info not provided; classification may not show 1st yr.

name: Geographical Adjustment
description: Rates for timekeepers in major metropolitan areas adjusted to rates for equally qualified timekeepers in same firm with offices in less expensive metropolitan areas.
notes: Requires office location and benchmark rates, not in schema.

name: Insourcing Opportunity
description: Reflects recurring, low value/low risk work best redeploy to alternative lower cost provider.
notes: Need to infer low-value recurring work and suitability for insourcing; NLP.

name: Multiple Attorney Call
description: More than one timekeeper bills for same telephonic call without client pre-approval.
notes: Need to detect same call across TKs using date/time and similar narratives.

name: Media Statement
description: Media Statements made by Outside Counsel on behalf of Client
notes: Keyword/phrase detection in narrative (press release, media statement).

name: Multi-Staffed Meetings
description: Meeting or conference attended by more than one timekeeper
notes: Need to recognize meetings in text and match across TKs on date/time.

name: Multi-Teaming
description: Two timekeepers at same level with the same area of expertise should not handle the identical task within same time frame
notes: Need same-level TKs doing same task; demands semantic task matching.

name: Outside Expertise
description: Timekeeper researches or must become educated on matters outside of timekeeper's core focus or area of practice
notes: Need TK specialty and topic in narrative; specialty is not explicit.

name: Other State Law
description: Timekeeper undertakes task involving the law of another jurisdiction in which timekeeper is not licensed.
notes: Need TK bar states and law jurisdiction mentioned; external data required.

name: Paralegal Task
description: Attorney level personnel should spend minimal time on tasks typically delegated to paralegals (docketing, preparation of entity formation documents, document review, bate stamping).
notes: Need to classify task as paralegal-type from narrative and identify attorney TK.

name: Personnel Transition Inefficiencies
description: Time associated with a transitioning timekeeper becoming familiar with a new matter
notes: Need to infer ramp-up/familiarization work and TK change history; semantic.

name: Pyramiding
description: Legal professional rate should not be charged for task(s) not requiring legal training, knowledge or judgment (e.g., reviewing newspaper articles re: lawsuit)
notes: Need to infer if task requires legal skill; text-based legal vs non-legal.

name: Research Memo
description: Memorialization of Legal Research in Written Medium
notes: Detect memo-writing about research via keywords in description.

name: Routine Motion Practice
description: Routine motions should prepared by very junior personnel with a modest level of review by non-junior personnel (e.g., agreed upon motion, notice of deposition, etc)
notes: Need to detect routine motions and see staffing mix and levels; narrative-driven.

name: Summer Associate Charge
description: No charge for summer associates
notes: If classification indicates summer associate and amount>0, flag.

name: Skill Set Mismatch Overqualified
description: Activities flagged when falls below timekeeper's experience level.
notes: Need to infer task complexity vs seniority; semantic interpretation.

name: Skill Set Mismatch Under Qualified
description: Activities flagged when tasks exceeds timekeeper's level of experience.
notes: Need to judge if task too complex for TK level from narrative.

name: Transitory Professional
description: Highlights line item entries by non-core team members.
notes: Must distinguish core vs non-core team from hours/patterns; heuristic, not exact.

name: Unsupervised Associate
description: Matters where junior attorneys or non-attorney have disproportionately large number of billable hours without apparent partner oversight or involvement.
notes: Compare hours by juniors vs partners on same matter; define partner via class.

name: Under Leveraged Matter
description: Matter staffing should use well leveraged mix of partners and associates for optimal cost efficiency.
notes: Analyze hours mix by role level per matter; threshold-based rule possible.

name: Churning File
description: Timekeeper repeatedly undertakes seemingly legitimate tasks which adds marginal value for client (e.g., repeated updates of corporate minute book, checking dockets, updating form contracts).
notes: Need to interpret task value and repetition over time; semantic and temporal.

name: Chipping
description: Less productive senior level timekeepers often serve as a "sounding board" burying small time charges within a larger matter.
notes: Need to find frequent small senior entries with vague advice narratives.

name: Excessive Research
description: Legal research occurs in an hourly amount in excess of client's guidelines for pre-approval.
notes: Need client research-hour cap, not provided; also must identify research work.

name: Excessive Time
description: Time for a repeated or routine task (e.g., first draft of form lease for multi-unit residential apartments, draft of UCC-1 ) exceeds industry norms for similarly experienced timekeepers.
notes: Requires external norms and semantic task classification to judge excess.

name: Grazing
description: Senior timekeepers record hours when "shadowing" another partner or keeping abreast of matters without incremental value add to a client.
notes: Need to infer shadowing/monitoring vs substantive work using text.

name: Local Counsel Engagement
description: Cost of interviewing and retention of local counsel where lead counsel strategically directs matter to a jurisdiction where it is unlicensed.
notes: Need to see narrative about hiring/engaging local counsel; text-based.

name: Legal Opinion Inflation
description: Multiple senior level attorneys record time for the preparation and review of a legal opinion.
notes: Need to identify legal opinion work and multiple seniors involved; NLP.

name: Office Communication
description: Excessive internal office conferences, meetings or other communications between and among outside counsel.
notes: Must detect internal communications in text and assess excess frequency.

name: Remedial Work
description: Identifies remedial or corrective work due to law firm errors
notes: Need narrative cues like correct, revise due to error; semantic judgment.

name: Repeated Task
description: Natural language processing tool detects repeated activity(ies) or category(ies) of activities which occurs with unusual frequency
notes: Explicitly NLP-based grouping of activities and frequency analysis.

name: Recycled Work Product
description: Indentifies time entries where modifications to forms and templates are billed as if work product was created anew.
notes: Need to see references to templates/forms and compare with prior work; NLP.

name: Small Incremental Communications
description: Small, repeating communications over time
notes: Need to detect brief communications and repetition using text and units.

name: Status Update
description: Narrative entries reflect an unusually high occurence of status updates for a client
notes: Identify status-update narratives and count frequency per client; NLP.

name: Tax Attorney
description: Identifies involvement of tax attorney in matters which are not taxation-centric.
notes: Need to know TK is tax specialist and whether matter work is tax-related from text.

name: Travel Time
description: Travel time should not be charged or discounted
notes: Detect travel-related entries via narrative and then apply discount rule.
